title: Finite-algebra dual-coalgebra and module/comodule category data
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $E$ an associative unital $k$-algebra, not assumed commutative, and put $D=\operatorname{Hom}_k(E,k)$. Use tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For a counital coassociative $k$-coalgebra structure $c=(\Delta,\epsilon)$ on $D$, the dual-algebra pairing predicate means $\langle\Delta d,a\otimes b\rangle=d(ab)$ and $\epsilon(d)=d(1)$ for all $d,a,b$, where $\langle f\otimes g,a\otimes b\rangle=f(a)g(b)$. A right coaction on a $k$-vector space $M$ is a linear map $\rho:M\to M\otimes_kD$ satisfying $(\rho\otimes1_D)\rho=(1_M\otimes\Delta)\rho$ and $(1_M\otimes\epsilon)\rho=1_M$, using the canonical associator and unitor. Finite-dimensional vector spaces mean finite spanning sets [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. The category of finite-dimensional left $E$-modules has objects a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $M$ with a unital $k$-algebra homomorphism $\alpha:E\to\operatorname{End}_k(M)$; its morphisms $M\to N$ are the $k$-linear maps $f$ satisfying $f(\alpha(a)m)=\beta(a)f(m)$ for all $a,m$. The category of finite-dimensional right $(D,c)$-comodules has objects finite-dimensional $M$ with such a right coaction, and morphisms the $k$-linear maps $f$ satisfying $(f\otimes1_D)\rho_M=\rho_N f$. Both categories have identity and composition given by the underlying linear maps, and their forgetful functors to finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces retain the underlying spaces and maps. Zero algebras and zero spaces are allowed. This definition asserts no existence of a coalgebra structure on $D$.
